statement: Two-dimensional Erdos-Turan-Koksma inequality with main term N/H. For points z_0, ..., z_{N-1} on the torus, H >= 7, and every half-open box [a,b) x [c,d) with b - a <= 1 and d - c <= 1, |#{n < N : z_n in box} - N (b-a)(d-c)| <= 32N/(H+1) + 2 sum w(k) w(l) |S_{k,l}|, the sum over (k,l) != (0,0) with |k|, |l| <= H, where S_{k,l} = sum_n e(k x_n + l y_n) and w(k) = 1/max(1,|k|). The proof smooths with the product Fejer kernel at radius 4/(H+1) and compares translates of the expanded and contracted boxes with the extreme box discrepancy, as in the one-dimensional BTCalculus.ErdosTuran; the double kernel integral is written as two nested one-dimensional integrals. This is the discrepancy input of Paper B Proposition 3.2; J-paper-b-proposition-3-2 uses it.

Paper B Proposition 3.2 (the OE third letter), with explicit constants. For N >= 1 and w in {OEE, OEO}, |#{n <= N : word_3(n) = w} - N/8| <= 6849 N^{5/6} (1 + log N). An odd start n has word OE. exactly when floor(n^{3/2}) is even, and floor(sqrt(floor x)) = floor(sqrt x) makes its third letter the parity of floor(n^{3/4}); each word is a box of area 1/4 for the torus point (n^{3/2}/2, n^{3/4}/2). On a block [a, a+M) of odd-start parameters with M <= a, the two-dimensional Erdos-Turan inequality (J-erdos-turan-koksma-box) at H = floor(a^{1/6}) and the second-derivative test bound the block discrepancy by 1712 a^{5/6} (1 + log a): for modes with i != 0 and |l| <= a^{3/4} the n^{3/4} curvature is at most a quarter of the n^{3/2} curvature, and the i = 0 modes use the n^{3/4} curvature alone. Halving at ceil(R/2) closes because (3/4)^{5/6} <= 4/5. The manuscript states O(N^{5/6} log(2N)); this is that statement with explicit constants.
